headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap makes prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files, use MCP, and ingest stdin/stdout; unstructured reads documents and text and writes files. A shared filesystem or copied outputs create a plausible injection bridge, though no direct automatic channel is documented. Because the pairwise interaction is only docs-based, uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document directory, then content from one can reach the other.
IF Gemini CLI is instructed to process files produced by unstructured, then file content can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Review files before passing them between agents.
Use a manual copy step with content sanitization.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, cwd files, shell environment, and broad network egress; unstructured handles documents, images, and text with allowlisted egress. If sensitive documents or code are shared through the same workspace, either agent can expose them to its backend or external endpoints. The profiles do not prove a shared OS workspace, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are mounted into both agents' working directories, then both can access them.
IF Gemini CLI is used on secrets or source code, then those contents may leave the local machine via network egress.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories.
Run each agent in a separate container or VM.
Restrict Gemini CLI to non-sensitive repos.
Use a redaction step before handing documents to unstructured.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, read the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; Gemini CLI also modifies git state. On a shared directory, concurrent edits can corrupt files or git history, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. This matches the high-risk overlap pattern because defaults are unsafe when both operate on the same repo.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, then concurrent writes can race.
IF Gemini CLI commits or rewrites git state while unstructured writes outputs into the same tree, then repository corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize access to the shared repo.
Disable git writes for one agent.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, and MCP-driven outputs; unstructured can consume documents and text and may treat upstream outputs as inputs. If unstructured ingests Gemini-produced artifacts without verification, errors can cascade into downstream parsing or transformation. The profiles do not show explicit authority to send emails or commit actions, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes Gemini CLI output as authoritative input, then upstream mistakes propagate.
IF Gemini CLI emits malformed or adversarial text into a document pipeline, then unstructured may parse it incorrectly.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Validate schemas before passing outputs onward.
Limit Gemini CLI to draft-only outputs.
Use checksum or signature checks on handoff files.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Gemini CLI explicitly handles a Google account login option and GEMINI_API_KEY, while unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints with document data. No PHI, EU-only, or residency mismatch is proven, so compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch and logging/retention uncertainty rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through both agents, then policy review is required.
IF either agent logs document contents or secrets beyond the intended retention window, then compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Disable optional account login for Gemini CLI.
Confirm privacy-policy terms before processing documents.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy.
